scope: Fourth-order Frontier-Science deductions from the unchanged EdgeBench v1 task scope, all 39 Science/ML design notes, the public Borden contract, and the absence of a reported independent-team treatment. These are proposed experiments, not EdgeBench empirical results.
source_facts: EdgeBench explicitly excludes tasks whose primary difficulty is visual understanding, to avoid confounding iterative reasoning with perception capability.
The full Science/ML design notes nevertheless include sensor-fault diagnosis, dirty GNSS processing, ECG preprocessing, PDF evidence extraction/meta-analysis, and satellite-image active learning.
The public Borden task supplies noisy censored monitoring data but its authoritative endpoint reads a fitted answer.json rather than replaying a complete raw-input method on fresh aquifers.

EdgeBench tasks predeclare objectives and judges, and the reported main experiments evaluate one agent trajectory per run rather than a randomized independent-investigator and blinded-synthesis treatment.

sle_experiments.design: Pair oracle-clean, frozen-reference and agent-built raw-instrument pipelines on identical latent worlds and common noise, with calibration, missingness, censoring, channel faults and true-anomaly controls.
Generate unit, coordinate, channel, grid, spectral and symmetry-equivalent metamorphic twins plus non-equivalent physical negative controls; canonicalize outputs after execution.

At equal total budgets compare a single agent, shared branches, isolated investigators, blinded evidence synthesis and a shared-context critic; require one signed team conclusion before fresh confirmation.

Freeze a domain-valid utility family, reveal constraints but draw weights only after signed commit, and compare public-scalar artifacts with reusable Pareto, response-surface or executable-method artifacts.

portfolio_priority.reason: Adds evidence synthesis, duplicate/selective-reporting detection, uncertainty, next-study design and prospective confirmation rather than another near-duplicate clean-simulator scalar optimization task.

claim_boundary: No new EdgeBench performance result is claimed.
Until I6 is run, the primary benchmark scope remains structured-observation science rather than instrument-facing autonomous science.
Until V4 is run, held-out score transfer does not establish unit, coordinate or representation robustness.
Until T1 is run, parallel candidates or shared-context critics do not establish independent scientific replication or team benefit.
Until U1 is run, optimizing a public scalar does not establish reusable value across legitimate downstream scientific utilities.
